mainEntity.name: How many Greek islands should I do in ten nights?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two, comfortably. Three if you're willing to give up a morning to each move. Two islands with a long stay on each almost always beats three with a rushed one.

In the Cyclades, the ones worth flying into are Santorini and Mykonos. Paros and Milos have small airports served mainly from Athens. Folegandros and Sifnos have none at all — they are reached by ferry, which is part of why they stay quiet.

mainEntity.name: Should I start or finish on Santorini?

acceptedAnswer.text: Finish. Santorini is the crescendo, and ending there means the caldera hotels are the last thing you remember rather than the bar everything else is measured against. It also opens up availability, because you're no longer tied to the properties with space on day one.

mainEntity.name: Can I take a ferry the same day I fly?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can, and I don't book it that way. Cycladic ferries cancel for wind with little notice, and a cancelled ferry on a flight day turns into a missed flight. I leave a night of margin between the last crossing and the flight home.

mainEntity.name: How long are the ferries between these islands?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mykonos to Paros is about 45 to 60 minutes. Santorini to Folegandros is about 45 minutes. Santorini to Milos and Paros to Santorini are both around two hours on a high-speed boat. None of these is a travel day — it's a morning.
